newsitem.title: JAPAN: WTO's Ruggiero upbeat on China's WTO entry talks.
newsitem.headline: WTO's Ruggiero upbeat on China's WTO entry talks.

text.p: The director-general of the World Trade Organisation (WTO), Renato Ruggiero, told Japanese business leaders on Friday that the WTO's talks with China on its entry into the world trade body were going well.

Ruggiero was quoted as saying by an official of the Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) that China and the WTO had made substantial progress in recent talks and he was upbeat about the negotiations.
Ruggiero said the talks were going in a good direction, but there were still issues to be resolved, the official said, adding that Ruggiero did not elaborate on those issues.

Beijing's bid to join the WTO has been held up partly because it wants to join on the easier terms accorded to a developing country. Some Western nations, including the United States, insist China's economy is too big for such treatment.
Ruggiero met about 50 to 60 business leaders belonging to Keidanren's trade and investment committee on Friday morning.

Asked about the WTO's stance in cases where national interests clash with multilateral rules as in the issue over the Helms-Burton law, Ruggiero said that the WTO's trade rules had been agreed and adopted by the member states, the Keidanren official said.
"I think he suggested by his comments that (the WTO's) rules had priority," the Keidanren official said.

The WTO has set up a panel to discuss the row between the European Union and the United States over the Helms-Burton law, which aims to stop non-American firms from investing in Cuba by leaving them open to prosecution in U.S. courts and by refusing to grant visas to their executives to visit the United States.

Asked about the possibility of getting private businesses involved in dispute settlement talks, Ruggiero said that the WTO was an organisation made up of various governments, but suggested that the issue may be raised in the future, the official said.
